endpoints.summary: Record a producer's or distributor's FBO-status attestation at onboarding

nfr_trace.boundary_condition: Attestation must be tied to an authenticated producer/distributor identity
Retain 6 years from creation, per Group Records Retention Policy

endpoints.reasoning: Formalised from HLD API-01 rather than derived: method, auth and the AttestationRequest/Attestation schema pair come from the HLD, and the Attestation entity's fields become components/schemas/Attestation with the Producer relationship as a $ref. The path gains the /v1 prefix the REST conventions require, which the HLD's /attestations lacks. Confidence is higher than the derive-from-scratch path because the shape arrives already vetted at qg-L1-hld-quality. The FR link comes from requirements.md — the HLD's own implements_features says F-01.1, a feature id this contract's traceability cannot use.

nfr_trace.boundary_condition: Retain 6 years from creation, per Group Records Retention Policy

endpoints.reasoning: Not seeded from the HLD, which has no read operation for attestations — derived from FR-001's ES3 retention condition, since a record retained 6 years is unverifiable without a read path. Emitted rather than suppressed because it has a genuine FR trace; the fact that the HLD lacks it is a real disagreement between the two surfaces and is raised as OQ-04, not silently resolved by dropping the operation.

endpoints.summary: Discover onboarded producers and distributors by category, location, and completeness score

nfr_trace.boundary_condition: Search results must show compliance-documentation completeness score alongside each producer
Buyer search/discovery response time — TBD — needs stakeholder input
Producer compliance documents, allergen declarations and individual completeness scores are Confidential

endpoints.reasoning: Formalised from HLD API-02; the Producer entity's fields become components/schemas/Producer and its completenessScore satisfies FR-002's Usability condition directly. The HLD's ProducerPage response is replaced with the conventions' cursor envelope, since the HLD does not specify a pagination strategy and the conventions do. The TBD latency stays as x-open-question (OQ-01).

fr_coverage.rationale: createAttestation formalises HLD API-01; getAttestation is derived from the ES3 retention condition, which the HLD does not address.
listProducers formalises HLD API-02, carrying all three discovery facets FR-002 names as query parameters.

open_questions.question: What response-time target should buyer producer-discovery search meet, and at which percentile?
How is the compliance-documentation completeness score defined and bounded — is it a 0-100 percentage, and what inputs determine it?

HLD API-03 (GET /producers/{producerId}/rating, buyer-satisfaction rating) traces to feature F-02.3 but to no functional requirement in requirements.md. Should a rating requirement be elicited, or should API-03 be dropped from the HLD?

GET /v1/attestations/{attestationId} is required by FR-001's 6-year retention condition but has no counterpart in the HLD. Should the HLD add a read operation to onboarding-service, or is attestation retrieval expected to happen outside the API?

artifacts.name: openapi.yaml
artifacts.description: OpenAPI 3.1 contract formalised from hld.md and reconciled against it — 3 operations across 2 resources

content.execution_summary:
• Produced 3 operations across 2 resources, formalised from the HLD's apis[] rather than derived from scratch: HLD API-01 and API-02 became createAttestation and listProducers, and the HLD's Attestation and Producer entities became components/schemas with the many-to-one Producer relationship as a $ref.
• FR coverage: 2 of 2 covered, none non_api.
• HLD reconciliation: 4 entries, 2 clean and 2 disagreeing in opposite directions. HLD API-03 (producer rating) traces to feature F-02.3 but to no FR, so it was NOT emitted — an endpoint with no FR behind it is an orphan regardless of which upstream document proposes it — and the disagreement is raised as OQ-03. Conversely getAttestation is required by FR-001's ES3 retention condition and has no HLD counterpart, so it WAS emitted, with the gap raised as OQ-04. Neither was silently resolved in either direction.
• Traceability note: the HLD's implements_features carries F-XX.X feature ids, not FR-NNN. Every fr_trace above comes from requirements.md; the two id vocabularies were not treated as interchangeable, which is why API-03's F-02.3 could not stand in for a missing FR.
• Where the conventions overrode the HLD: /v1 path prefix added (the HLD's paths are unversioned), and the HLD's ProducerPage response replaced with the cursor-pagination envelope, the HLD specifying no pagination strategy.
• Open questions: 4 — one nfr_tbd (OQ-01), one requirements_gap (OQ-02), two hld_reconciliation (OQ-03, OQ-04). OQ-03 is the only one with source_fr '—', which is itself the finding: it has no FR to point at.
• Self-check: FR sets in requirements.md and nfr-spec.md compared first — 2 ids, same order, matched. Every emitted operation carries >=1 fr_trace; every FR has exactly one fr_coverage entry; every HLD API-NN and every openapi.yaml path appears in hld_reconciliation.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-enterprise-security (ES1 external-IdP scheme — consistent with the HLD's own cross_cutting.identity, ES2 Confidential classification, ES3 6-year retention); kb-L1-enterprise-architecture (EA2/EA4 Gateway-published — consistent with the HLD's cross_cutting.gateway: Kong; EA3 the HLD's SMDS integration confirmed read-only, no write-back).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-output-schema-validator (pass), gr-L1-hallucination-check (pass), gr-L1-consistency-check (pass), gr-L1-schema-validator-openapi (not run — not yet built).
• Artifact saved to s3://adlc-artifacts/exec-77dd88ee/openapi.yaml.
• Gaps flagged: OQ-03 and OQ-04 need an HLD-owner decision before L1-design-lld consumes either document, or the two artifacts will disagree downstream.
